prompt:
Write the appraiser's remarks (about 80 words) on a body shop repair estimate after a hit while turning left. Describe the damage seen on the vehicle and the repair plan. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1009; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- Two similar charges on the same day are being checked.
- The repair labor hours fit the damage.
- Records show the same major damage from an earlier, unreported accident; it is now claimed as new.
text: The rear quarter panel and bumper cover show crush and tear patterns that line up well with the impact described for a left turn collision. The estimated labor hours match the extent of the repairs, and the parts list follows the damage as recorded. Two similar charges entered on the same day are under review before approval. Shop records also show comparable major damage on the same panels from an earlier accident that was never reported, and the current claim presents that prior damage as new. Recommend holding payment on the affected items until the prior repair history is verified and the two charges are reconciled. Remaining items can proceed once that review is complete.
